selected_script.angle: Absurd firefighter grandfather rescuing a bursting carry-on backpack before a business trip
selected_script.hook: Close-up of a traveler desperately sitting on a bulging carry-on backpack, popping zippers and spilling bulky jackets

script_record.pain_point: Bulky winter clothing taking up 90% of carry-on backpack space, preventing zippers from closing
script_record.conflict_hook: Traveler jumping on a bulging backpack on the bed as zippers split open
script_record.product_solution: Grandfather in full firefighter gear attaches white cordless pump to transparent honeycomb vacuum bag valve, deflating it flat in seconds

timeline.scene: Close-up of traveler sitting heavily on a bulging backpack on a bed, struggling and failing to force the zipper shut.

timeline.purpose: 荒诞成年亲属携产品入场
timeline.scene: An absurd grandfather wearing full yellow firefighter gear strides in holding the transparent vacuum bag and white cordless pump, yelling 'I got this!'
Grandfather places packed clothes into transparent honeycomb clear bag, seals double zipper, and attaches white electric pump; bag shrinks down instantly saving 80% space.
Fast cut 1: The ultra-flat compressed vacuum bag slides effortlessly into the carry-on luggage with room to spare.
Fast cut 2: Traveler easily packing five compressed bags into a small suitcase for a weekend business trip.
Fast cut 3: Neat closet shelf storage with multiple neatly stacked honeycomb mesh vacuum bags.
Clean product display shot with CTA text overlay: 'Triple your luggage space today.'

final_moyin_jobs.promptText:
Create a 10-second vertical UGC ad video.
Timeline:
0-1.5s: Show one real daily pain point through a close-up detail. Traveler desperately trying to force close a bulging carry-on backpack on a bedroom bed, zipper splitting open. No product and no rescuer.
1.5-3s: An absurd grandfather in full yellow firefighter gear enters carrying the exact product (transparent clear vacuum bag with honeycomb grid and white cylindrical rechargeable air pump) from the first frame, takes it directly to the bed, and says 'I got this!'.
3-6s: Quickly show the product as the direct solution. Clothes are sealed inside the double-zip transparent bag, white pump attached to the dark grey valve, deflating the bag flat in seconds.
6-10s: Fast-cut scene 1 showing the first clear result: sliding the flat compressed bag neatly into a carry-on suitcase.
Do not start with a perfect product shot. Do not end with a CTA in this segment. Keep the pacing fast, clear, low-risk, and product-focused.
Use the provided product reference images as the exact product identity. Do not change the product color, shape, material, size ratio, logo position, texture, or visible structure. Do not invent extra accessories, buttons, lights, packaging, or exaggerated functions.
Use the detail and side reference image to preserve product material, side structure, edge shape, texture, and visible details.
Use the function reference image only to understand the real product usage. Do not invent new functions.
